extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/anabelian geometry familiar with Mochizuki's IUT
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and understanding the named logical principles, structural distinctions, and diagnostic criteria Mochizuki uses to describe the logical architecture of inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT) and to diagnose typical misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: (RCΘ1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas the (Θ±ellNF-)Hodge theaters in the domain and codomain of the Θ-link in inter-universal Teichmüller theory are isomorphic, i.e., if one does not require any sort of compatibility of the isomorphism, in the evident sense, with the Θ-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to contrast the trivial isomorphism-of-objects perspective (ignoring compatibility with the Θ-link) with the more constrained, compatibility-respecting notion required in the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: (RCΘ2)
rubrics_metrics.description: As observed in Example 3.2.2, (i-a), (iv) — essentially as a consequence of the definition of a ring, i.e., the elementary observation that the N-th power map, for an integer N ≥ 2, on a domain of generic characteristic zero is not a ring homomorphism — these domain and codomain (Θ±ellNF-)Hodge theaters do not admit an isomorphism that is compatible, in the evident sense, with the Θ-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains a concrete obstruction (non-ring-homomorphism of N-th power map) to existence of compatibility-respecting isomorphisms; clarifies that compatible isomorphisms fail in relevant examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: (RCΘ2lg)
rubrics_metrics.description: The property discussed in (RCΘ2) ... is never logically applied in the development or proofs of the main results [such as, for instance, [IUTchIII], Theorem 3.11, or [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12] of inter-universal Teichmüller theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation: even if one is unsure whether (RCΘ2) holds, this uncertainty does not affect the essential logical structure of the main results; at worst it indicates possible 'overkill' in the argument but not a foundational dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: (RCΘ3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagrams in the two displays of (ii) yield a situation analogous to (RCRS3) in the sense that neither the pairs ... are isomorphic, i.e., regardless of whether or not one imposes a compatibility condition ... with the [analogue of the] Θ-link; in particular, this situation yields interesting counterexamples to the analogue ... of the Neukirch-Uchida Theorem for number fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to point out that certain domain/codomain pairs are non-isomorphic even when ignoring compatibility, leading to counterexamples to naive analogues of classical reconstruction theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: (StrDf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the observation of (RCΘ3) is of independent interest in its own right ... relative to the analogy discussed in (TltSim), the sorts of pairs considered in (RCΘ3) are completely useless from the point of view of constructing any sort of theory using these pairs that is in some sense structurally analogous to inter-universal Teichmüller theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/interpretation: stresses which kinds of object-pairs are irrelevant or unhelpful for building IUT-analogous theories; highlights structural differences that matter for IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: TltDf3
rubrics_metrics.description: The positive characteristic nature of k(cid:7) means that k(cid:7) does not admit any sort of evident analogue of the p-adic logarithm, which is fundamental to the definition of the log-link in inter-universal Teichmüller theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists a structural limitation arising from positive characteristic fields: lack of a p-adic logarithm analogue; important when judging applicability of constructions relying on log-links.

rubrics_metrics.name: TltDf4
rubrics_metrics.description: The positive characteristic nature of k(cid:7) means that k(cid:7) does not admit any sort of evident analogue of the pro-p portion of the theory of cyclotomic rigidity surrounding the theta function, as well as local and global fields, all of which plays a fundamental role in inter-universal Teichmüller theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains another structural obstruction in positive characteristic obstructing the cyclotomic rigidity tools central to IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: TltDf5
rubrics_metrics.description: Any situation such as the one described in (RCΘ3) — i.e., where the topological fields in the domain and codomain of the [analogue of the] Θ-link are not isomorphic — necessarily fails to satisfy, even at the level of étale-like objects, the symmetry property discussed in Example 3.2.2, (ii-c), (iv), which plays a fundamental role in inter-universal Teichmüller theory (for establishing multiradiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that lack of field isomorphism obstructs key symmetry properties needed for multiradial representation; practical criterion when evaluating candidate examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: TltDf6
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-locally compact nature of perfectoid fields (i.e., the non-openness discussed in (TltDf1)) means that fields such as k, †k, ‡k do not admit any sort of evident analogue of the phenomenon of compatibility of cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms with the profinite/tempered topology, which plays a fundamental role in inter-universal Teichmüller theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns about limits of transferring arguments from locally compact/profinite settings to perfectoid contexts; criterion to check when porting constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TltDf7
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-locally compact nature of perfectoid fields ... means that these fields do not admit any sort of evident analogue of the notion of log-volume, which plays a fundamental role in IUT; in particular, there is no evident analogue of the notion of log-volume on finite subextensions of Qp contained in †k, ‡k that can be shared in a consistent fashion between the domain and codomain of isomorphisms as in the diagram of the second display of (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies absence of log-volume analogues as an obstruction; important when assessing whether numeric/log-volume based arguments transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Syp1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sense of unjustified and acutely harsh abruptness in the passage from [IUTchIII], Theorem 3.11, to [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic criterion: if a reader feels abruptness in that passage, that is a typical symptom of misunderstanding the logical structure; suggests locating where AND-relations are being lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Syp2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to see the 'proof' of some sort of commutative diagram or 'compatibility property' to the effect that taking log-volumes of pilot objects in the domain and codomain of the Θ-link yields the same real number (a property which, in fact, can never be proved since it is false!).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic: attempting to force equality of log-volumes is misguided; signals misunderstanding of the IUT approach and of what can be proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Syp3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to see the inequality of the final numerical estimate obtained as the result of concatenating some chain of intermediate inequalities, as is often done in proofs in real/complex/functional analysis or analytic number theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic: expecting a chain-of-inequalities derivation is incorrect for IUT; indicates a category error about the theory's logical architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: (∧-Chn)
rubrics_metrics.description: The logical structure of inter-universal Teichmüller theory proceeds by observing a chain of AND relations '∧'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core principle: instead of concatenating inequalities, IUT builds and preserves explicit chains of logical AND-relations; this reframes how one should track information through the multiradial algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: (∧-Dgns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine precisely where in the finite sequence of steps that appear is the first step at which the person feels that the preservation of the crucial AND relator '∧' is no longer clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical diagnostic procedure: to analyze misunderstandings, identify the earliest step at which the reader loses sight of preservation of AND-relations; use the finite-step nature of the multiradial algorithm to localize confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: (∧-Input)
rubrics_metrics.description: The input data for this multiradial algorithm consists solely of an abstract F (cid:2)(cid:3)×μ-prime-strip; moreover, this multiradial algorithm is functorial with respect to arbitrary isomorphisms between such prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides what initial data the multiradial algorithm accepts and how functoriality means it may be applied uniformly; important when checking whether a purported input is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: (ExtInd)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle of extension of indeterminacies: If A, B, and C are propositions, then A ∧ B =⇒ A ∧ (B ∨ C) (since B ⇒ B ∨ C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central logical move used throughout the multiradial algorithm to derive new AND-relations from old ones by enlarging indeterminacy (introducing OR). Explains why introduction of OR-relations is inherent and necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: (ExtInd1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations that consist of simply adding more possibilities/indeterminacies (which corresponds to passing from B to B ∨ C) within some fixed container.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical uses include establishing symmetry/invariance properties (e.g., upper semi-continuity, passage to holomorphic hulls); viewed as preparing descent data prior to identifying labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: (ExtInd2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations in which one identifies ('crushes together', by passing from B to B ∨ C) objects with distinct labels, at the cost of passing to a situation in which the object is regarded as being only known up to isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewed as the actual descent operation: after preparing via ExtInd1, one collapses labels to move from label-dependent data to label-independent data (up to isomorphism). Examples include identifying Πv's at different vertical coordinates or identifying Gv's at different coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: (sQLTL)
rubrics_metrics.description: One wishes to apply (ExtInd) to form '(sub)quotients/splittings' of the log-theta-lattice, i.e., to project the vertical line on the left-hand side of the infinite 'H' portion of the log-theta-lattice onto the vertical line on the right-hand side of this infinite 'H' by somehow achieving some sort of 'crushing together' of distinct coordinates (i.e., '(n, m)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the geometric/log-lattice aim behind applying ExtInd: how label-crushing is used concretely to obtain the relevant (sub)quotients in the log-theta-lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: (ExtInd) typical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical examples of (ExtInd1) include the upper semi-continuity of (Ind3), as well as the passage to holomorphic hulls. Typical examples of (ExtInd2) are identifying 'Πv's at different vertical coordinates, identifying 'Gv's at different coordinates, and identifying F×μ-prime-strips arising from Θ- and q-pilot objects in distinct Hodge theaters by working up to isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete instances of both flavors of ExtInd to help recognize them in proofs; helpful for checking which step of an argument is doing which kind of extension/identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poly-morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Poly-morphisms — sets of morphisms between objects — appear throughout IUT as a tool for facilitating the explicit enumeration of a collection of possibilities. Composable ordered pairs may be composed by composing their constituent morphisms; poly-morphisms enumerate possibilities related via OR relations '∨'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use poly-morphisms to record indeterminacies and produce symmetry/invariance properties needed for descent. Classical examples: homotopy classes of maps, morphisms in derived categories, orbits under group actions. They relate directly to gluing constructions (e.g., algebraic stacks).

rubrics_metrics.name: (∧(∨)-Chn)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential logical structure of IUT may be understood as iteratively turning A ∧ B into A ∧ (B1 ∨ B2 ∨ ...) and then enlarging/iterating those OR-collections, producing nested ORs that maintain the crucial AND with A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the combinatorial/logical pattern of repeatedly applying ExtInd and poly-morphism composition to build the multiradial chain while preserving key AND-relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitability of inner automorphism indeterminacies (Example 3.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functoriality of the étale fundamental group only holds if one allows for inner automorphism indeterminacies; concrete Galois-extension examples show automorphisms that act nontrivially on a normal subgroup and produce outer automorphism indeterminacies on quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural criterion: when relating étale fundamental groups via functoriality, expect and accept inner (and induced outer) automorphism indeterminacies; attempts to eliminate them are generally impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: (NoSpl)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surjection GFmod → Γmod of profinite groups does not admit a splitting; equivalently, the natural outer action of ΓGal_mod does not admit a lifting to an action free of inner automorphism indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete obstruction used in the construction of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters: explains why certain group actions necessarily carry inner automorphism ambiguity and cannot be made strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: (NoSyn)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no well-defined synchronization between these copies of Gv that is free of inner automorphism (conjugacy) indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical constraint: attempting to synchronize local Galois copies across distinct prime-strips without conjugacy ambiguity is impossible; one must instead impose isolation procedures (LGIsl).

rubrics_metrics.name: (LGIsl) local-global isolation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the local absolute Galois group Gv are to be regarded not as subgroups of some global absolute Galois group, but rather as coric objects treated as independent of any embedding into a global absolute Galois group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive structural requirement for constructing Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters: isolate local data from global absolute Galois structure to avoid unwanted inner-automorphism indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: (SymIsl)
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue of isolating the F(cid:3)±_l-symmetry from the F(cid:2)_l-symmetry in order to achieve conjugate synchronization is one important reason for imposing the local-global isolation requirement (LGIsl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains a motivation for LGIsl: separate additive and multiplicative symmetry portions to allow conjugate synchronization via the desired symmetry group.

rubrics_metrics.name: (SctNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even within the multiplicative symmetry portion of a (Θ±ellNF-)Hodge theater, the goal of simulating a global canonical generator requires one to treat the various prime-strips that appear in the multiplicative symmetry portion as 'sections', in some suitable sense, of the finite étale quotient Spec(K) → Spec(Fmod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical prescription about how to regard prime-strips when simulating global generators: they should function like sections of an étale quotient to achieve the simulation.
